s: A company is in the process of implementing AWS Organizations to constrain its developers to use only Amazon EC2. Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB. The developers account resides In a dedicated organizational unit (OU). The solutions architect has implemented the following SCP on the developers account: When this policy is deployed, IAM users in the developers account are still able to use AWS services that are not listed in the policy. What should the solutions architect do to eliminate the developers' ability to use services outside the scope of this policy?
o: Create an explicit deny statement for each AWS service that should be constrained
Remove the Full AWS Access SCP from the developer account's OU
Modify the Full AWS Access SCP to explicitly deny all services
Add an explicit deny statement using a wildcard to the end of the SCP

w.y: SCPs only filter permissions, and a permission must be allowed by an SCP at every level. While the default FullAWSAccess SCP remains attached to the OU, it allows everything, so an allow-list SCP for EC2, S3 and DynamoDB restricts nothing. Detaching FullAWSAccess makes the allow list effective.

o.A: Denying each unwanted service individually is unmanageable and misses new services.
o.B: Correct: removing FullAWSAccess leaves only the allow-list SCP, so unlisted services are implicitly denied.
o.C: Editing the AWS-managed FullAWSAccess policy is not possible, and denying all services would block the allowed ones too.
o.D: A wildcard explicit deny would override the allows and block EC2, S3 and DynamoDB as well.

s: Inheritance for authorization policies - AWS Organizations

nt: The SCP in the stem was an image in the PDF and is missing. The point: SCPs are filters. While the FullAWSAccess SCP stays attached, an allow-list SCP restricts nothing, so remove FullAWSAccess (B).
